extracted.intended_audience: JOSS handling editors, Track Editors-in-Chief, and volunteer editors
extracted.subtask_description: Operational editorial workflow and acceptance criteria for handling submissions to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS), including pre-review screening gates, reviewer selection, review conduct, post-review publication checks, and special-case procedures (AAS collaboration, rOpenSci/pyOpenSci).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public development history ≥ 6 months (hard gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository must be public for more than six months with development activity distributed across that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recent repo dump or commits concentrated into a short window fails this gate. Check commit distribution over time, not just total commit count. Failure of this gate should trigger a desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated research impact (hard gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be evidence the software is actually being used for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for paper/preprint references, DOIs, cited use by others, or documented integration into research workflows. Potential future use is not sufficient. If missing, reject at pre-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open source practices (hard gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository must show expected signals of an open project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-author projects: presence of issues, pull requests, and public discussion. For single-author projects: at least several of tagged releases/changelog, tests/CI, clear documentation, a CONTRIBUTING file, and stated support expectations. Multiple indicators must be present. Single-author projects should not be rejected solely for lacking a PR workflow if other signals are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative development (hard gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit history should show ongoing refinement rather than a one-time code dump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the temporal distribution of commits to confirm iterative development. A one-off dump is a fail for this gate and can trigger a desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk-rejection for combined shortcomings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that do not clearly fail a single gate but fall short on several may be desk-rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When desk-rejecting in borderline cases, summarise the specific gaps in the rejection notice and encourage resubmission in six months once those gaps are addressed. See sample messages for rejection language.

rubrics_metrics.name: General description of the software (editor check)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission should include a general description of the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should verify that the paper/repository provides a clear overview of what the software does and its purpose before moving to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope as research software
rubrics_metrics.description: The software must be within JOSS's scope as research software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If out-of-scope, flag and notify the author in the PRE-REVIEW issue. Editors can use @editorialbot query scope to add a query-scope label. TEiC will make the final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSI-approved license required
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository must have an OSI-approved open-source license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should confirm the presence of such a license during the pre-review/editor check step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reviewer count
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must have at least two reviewers for JOSS review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: papers previously reviewed and accepted by rOpenSci or pyOpenSci. If unsure about a submission, recruit a third or fourth reviewer; having at least three is helpful if one drops out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Between the selected reviewers, all aspects of the submission should be covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that a single reviewer rarely covers all aspects (language proficiency vs. scientific domain). Aim that reviewers together cover code language, software engineering, and scientific discipline expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to JOSS conflict-of-interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection and assignment of reviewers must follow the JOSS COI policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify potential conflicts before assignment; do not assign reviewers with disqualifying conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should use multiple strategies to find and recruit reviewers and verify appropriateness of author-suggested reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reviewer volunteer list or Reviewers Management System, filter by language/domain expertise, use professional network, search literature/GitHub, ask authors for suggestions (but verify and do not allow authors to @-tag their suggestions). Avoid asking JOSS editors to review if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add reviewers via EditorialBot
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reviewer accepts, add them to the PRE-REVIEW issue using EditorialBot commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commands like @editorialbot add @username as reviewer. If starting the review before all reviewers are identified, hand-edit the checklist to add later reviewers after review start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start review with EditorialBot-generated REVIEW issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Run @editorialbot start review to create the REVIEW issue with prepared review checklists and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure editor and at least one reviewer are assigned before starting; move conversation to the REVIEW issue and instruct reviewers to generate/check their checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the review checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should generate and use the checklist (via @editorialbot generate my checklist) and check off items until done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items are the canonical record of review progress. New reviewers added after start must run the generate my checklist command to get their checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication norms in REVIEW issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments in the REVIEW issue should be kept brief; longer suggestions or requests should be posted as separate issues in the submission repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide link-backs to those repository issues in the REVIEW issue. The editor should 'lurk' and intervene if needed (e.g., for CoC issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unresponsive or recanting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer recants their commitment or is unresponsive, remove or replace them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @editorialbot remove @username from reviewers to remove. You can add new reviewers in the REVIEW issue as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer acceptance and recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers are satisfied with improvements, they should confirm their recommendation to accept the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should state acceptance in the REVIEW issue; the editor then pings the EiC team to get the paper published using @editorialbot recommend-accept when post-review steps are done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review: tagged release and archival deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should create a new tagged release and archive the software (e.g., Zenodo, figshare) when the software has changed during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors post the version number and archive DOI in the REVIEW issue. The editor sets the archive and version with EditorialBot commands (e.g., @editorialbot set <doi> as archive, set <version> as version). Note: a new release is only necessary if the software changed; changes to the paper do not require a new release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review: final checks and proofing
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should perform final pre-publication checks including generating proofs, checking references, and proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run @editorialbot create post-review checklist and @editorialbot generate pdf; use @editorialbot check references to verify references have DOIs where appropriate; proof-read the paper and ask authors to fix remaining typos, citations, or awkward wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive metadata and author list consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the archive deposit has correct metadata and that author lists in the archive and paper correspond appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically the two author lists should match; if there are differences, authors/editors should explain them. Check that all paper authors are present in the archive metadata and ask for reasons when they differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final publication handoff
rubrics_metrics.description: When everything looks good, the handling editor pings the TEiC/EiC team to process final publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @editorialbot recommend-accept to notify @openjournals/joss-eics that the paper is ready for final processing; EiC/AEiC will make final checks and publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting a paper: scope flagging and process
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission should be rejected (e.g., out-of-scope), flag the submission and communicate reasons to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use @editorialbot query scope to add query-scope label. Mention reasons for flagging and optionally give the author a chance to respond. TEiC will make the final determination; during scope review the team may request additional information from authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope review for resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: For resubmissions previously rejected, TEiC will decide whether to require a full scope review, whether prior reasons remain valid, or whether updates warrant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TEiC discretion guides whether the editorial team needs to re-run full scope review or accept/resume review based on submitted changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAS collaboration: additional labeling and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: For joint AAS publications, apply the AAS label and follow additional editorial steps including disclosure of a small donation from AAS publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the AAS label to both PRE-REVIEW and REVIEW issues, inform reviewers of the AAS donation before moving to review, request AAS DOI after acceptance and update paper.md YAML header with aas-doi and aas-journal, and pause the review (apply paused label) until notified that the AAS paper is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: rOpenSci/pyOpenSci streamlined acceptance path
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions already reviewed and accepted by rOpenSci or pyOpenSci follow a streamlined JOSS workflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign yourself as editor and reviewer, add comments and label pointing to the prior review, start the review issue, compile the paper and check it looks OK, grab the Zenodo DOI from the source repo, then accept and publish without full duplicate review.
